definitions.explanation: Two children born to the same mother at one birth. A formal, technical word; everyday speech uses {双子|ふたご}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一卵性|いちらんせい}→一卵性：08959_ichiransei⟧{双生児|そうせいじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
{双生児|そうせいじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{遺伝|いでん}→遺伝：10137_iden⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{扱|あつか}われる→扱う：01862_atsukau⟧。
examples.english: Twins are often studied in genetic research.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一卵性|いちらんせい}→一卵性：08959_ichiransei⟧{双生児|そうせいじ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{二卵性|にらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{遺伝子|いでんし}→遺伝子：05031_idenshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{共通|きょうつう}→共通：02590_kyoutsuu⟧⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧。
examples.english: Identical twins and fraternal twins differ in how much of their genes they share.

notes:
A formal, scholarly term of Chinese-character origin: {双|そう} (pair) + {生|せい} (birth) + {児|じ} (child). Used in medical, academic, and legal contexts; ordinary conversation uses ⟦{双子|ふたご}→双子：03599_futago⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{一卵性|いちらんせい}→一卵性：08959_ichiransei⟧{双生児|そうせいじ}: identical (monozygotic) twins
- {二卵性|にらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}: fraternal (dizygotic) twins
- {双生児|そうせいじ}⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧: twin study

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{双子|ふたご}→双子：03599_futago⟧: twins — the everyday word; {双生児|そうせいじ} is its formal counterpart
- ⟦{三|み}つ{子|ご}→三つ子：28184_mitsugo⟧: triplets — three children born together
